propositions: Pytest tests run detached via nohup report spurious errors that do not reproduce in foreground runs, causing investigators to chase phantom regressions.

The root cause is not detachment itself but concurrent external mutations (file creation, process reaping, git operations) to the shared checkout that the test isolation guards misattribute to tests and cannot distinguish from in-test leaks.

The _no_repo_root_leaks guard fires in teardown and deletes external entries it cannot attribute, silently destroying concurrent work; the browser e2e probe diagnostic reports signal-killed children without consulting returncode, making externally-reaped runs indistinguishable from product failures.

Detached runs are trustworthy when the checkout is not concurrently mutated, but this constraint is undocumented, and the guards' messages falsely assert test causation when external actors mutate the tree.
The isolation guard messages and browser probe diagnostic must be corrected to name the concurrent-external-process possibility and include child process returncode in error reports.
